title: Euclidean Geometry: Circle Theorems
summary: The circle theorems and their converses: perpendicular from the centre, angles at the centre and circumference, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals, tangents and the tan-chord theorem, with proofs and riders.

items: **Chord**: a line segment joining two points on a circle. A **diameter** is a chord through the centre.
**Arc**: part of the circumference. A chord **subtends** an angle at a point.
**Tangent**: a line that touches the circle at exactly one point.
**Cyclic quadrilateral**: a quadrilateral with all four vertices on a circle.

rows: The line from the centre perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc
The angle in a semicircle is a right angle
Angles in the same segment are equal
The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary
The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact
Two tangents drawn from the same point outside a circle are equal
The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment

notes.caption: Theorem 2: the angle AOB at the centre is twice the angle ACB at the circumference

notes.text: Converses: proving a quadrilateral is cyclic

items: One pair of opposite angles is supplementary (converse opp ∠s of cyclic quad).
An exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle (converse ext ∠ of cyclic quad).
A side subtends equal angles at the other two vertices (converse ∠s in the same seg).

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: O is the centre of the circle and $\hat{AOB} = 124^\circ$. C is on the major arc. Find $\hat{ACB}$ and, if D is on the minor arc AB, find $\hat{ADB}$.
steps: ACBD is a cyclic quadrilateral, so $\hat{ADB} = 180^\circ - 62^\circ = 118^\circ$ (opp ∠s of cyclic quad)

notes.title: Worked example 2: tangents
notes.problem: PA and PB are tangents to a circle with centre O. If $\hat{APB} = 50^\circ$, find $\hat{AOB}$ and $\hat{PAB}$.
steps: PA = PB (tans from same pt), so $\hat{PAB} = \hat{PBA} = \frac{180^\circ - 50^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ$ (∠s opp = sides)

notes.title: Worked example 3: perpendicular from the centre
notes.problem: A chord of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius.
steps: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving halves of 8 cm (line from centre ⊥ to chord).

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In riders, mark all known angles on your diagram as you go. Look for isosceles triangles formed by radii (radii are equal), and look for the tan-chord theorem whenever a tangent meets a chord.

questions.prompt: TA is a tangent to the circle at A. Chord AB makes $\hat{TAB} = 70^\circ$, and C is a point on the circle in the alternate segment. Find $\hat{ACB}$, and $\hat{AOB}$ if O is the centre. Give reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ $\hat{ACB} = 70^\circ$ (tan chord theorem) (2)
✓ $\hat{AOB} = 140^\circ$ (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circumference) (1)

questions.prompt: In quadrilateral PQRS, $\hat{P} = 2x$ and $\hat{R} = x + 60^\circ$. For which value of $x$ is PQRS cyclic? Give a reason.
questions.memo:
✓ For a cyclic quad, $\hat{P} + \hat{R} = 180^\circ$ (converse opp ∠s of cyclic quad) (1)
✓ $3x + 60^\circ = 180^\circ$ (1)
✓ $x = 40^\circ$ (1)

questions.prompt: O is the centre of a circle. A and B lie on the circle and $\hat{OAB} = 28^\circ$. Find $\hat{AOB}$ and the angle subtended by AB at a point C on the major arc.
questions.memo:
✓ $\hat{OBA} = 28^\circ$ (∠s opp equal radii) (1)
✓ $\hat{AOB} = 124^\circ$ (sum of ∠s in △) (1)
✓ $\hat{ACB} = 62^\circ$ (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circumference) (1)
